title: Add linter
lede: How /add-linter adds linter configs and CI workflows for the languages in a repo, without changing a config you already have until you approve a merge.

detect.name: Detect
detect.role: Find each language in the repo and whether it already has a linter config.
details: If every language is already current, it stops: nothing to do.

ask.name: Ask once
ask.role: One multi-select question covers every language that needs action.
details: If the user confirms none, nothing is written.

emit.name: Emit
emit.role: A deterministic CLI writes new configs and workflows, and never edits an existing config.

more: It writes the template beside it as a .scaffold-new sidecar.

details: Adopted configs (fresh or already current) add the linter's missing npm packages to package.json devDependencies; sidecars don't. js/ts also get lint and lint:fix scripts.
qs: Why does the CLI write a sidecar instead of editing my config?

merge.name: Merge
merge.role: The agent merges the sidecar into your config, keeping your rules, and writes only on approval.
details: Missing scaffold thresholds are added and the marker line is carried over.
On approval the original is backed up to .bak (an existing .bak is never overwritten) and the sidecar removed.
risks: On a conflict your value is kept and the conflict is listed, so you see what scaffold would have changed.

finish.name: Tune and commit
finish.role: Optionally match settings to your existing code, report per language, and offer to commit.
details: Tuning proposes values seen in your code, for example line length; you confirm, override or decline.
The commit never includes .bak or .scaffold-new files.

sidecar.d: A .scaffold-new copy saved beside your file for you to review and merge; your file is never overwritten.

marker.d: A hash-stamped line that tags a config as scaffold's.

threshold.d: A rule limit, such as max line length.

ask.context: The reader wants to understand how scaffold's /add-linter skill sets up linting for a repo without clobbering existing configs.
